title: Path library for extended-length paths and reserved device names
question_or_target: does a tree containing a file named NUL still enumerate completely, and what does the relative-path computation return for it?

library.relpath_algorithm: component-wise logical_abspath + safe_relpath; never os.path.relpath / GetFullPathNameW on reserved names
library.walk_fail_closed: WalkIncomplete is raised when errors exist and zero entries were collected; swallowing_walk_count is the defect replica

evidence.claim: Named probe 1 (source) and probe 2 (verifier) both ran live and exited 0 on this checkout.

negative_controls.description: [original kind: known-crash-replica] naive_windows_relpath raises ValueError on a file named NUL, matching os.path.relpath / GetFullPathNameW on Windows
negative_controls.bad_state_output: path is on mount '\\.\NUL', start on mount 'Z:'

negative_controls.description: [original kind: known-broken-enumerator] A walk that catches the reserved-name crash and returns [] reports zero entries; the library must not be equivalent

reviewer.notes: [note: Probe 2 is a mechanically different instrument: long-path round-trip plus the swallow-zero control, not a re-read of probe 1's reserved-name delta.]

notes: G-1 delivery for IMP-0467 on Linux: a tree containing a file named NUL enumerates completely (file count differs by exactly one versus the same tree without NUL; neither walk raises). safe_relpath returns 'NUL', not a \\.\NUL device mount. A long path above 260 characters is created, walked, and read back. The crash-swallowing enumerator returns 0; the library does not. SENTINEL:IMP-0467:PATH-LIBRARY-WINDOWS-SAFE

schema_repair_preserved.value: swallowing_walk_count returns 0 on the reserved tree; walk_tree returns the real non-zero file count
